title: Delta Air Lines 1141
summary: Delta Air Lines Flight 1141 crashed during takeoff from Dallas-Fort Worth on August 31, 1988. The crew failed to configure the aircraft's flaps and slats for takeoff, and the takeoff warning system malfunctioned. Immediately after liftoff, the aircraft experienced violent rolling and the right wing dropped, striking the runway and an ILS antenna array before being destroyed.
probable_cause: The crew's failure to configure the aircraft's flaps and slats for takeoff, combined with the malfunction of the takeoff configuration warning system which failed to alert the crew. Contributing factors included inadequate cockpit discipline, Delta's slow implementation of modifications to operating procedures and training, and insufficient FAA oversight.

factors.evidence: Crew engaged in extended casual conversations on non-flight matters during preflight and pushback phases (p. 72-75).
Aircraft attempted takeoff without flaps and slats extended to proper configuration (p. 58-60).
Takeoff warning system failed due to throttle switch contamination or misalignment (p. 60-62).
Immediate violent rolling after liftoff with right wing dropping (p. 6-7).
Right wingtip struck runway and ILS antenna array, causing structural breakup (p. 6-7).
Post-crash fire engulfed fuselage from leaking fuel (p. 7).

events.text: Flight 1141 departs Jackson, Mississippi gate; first officer to fly
Arrival at DFW gate 15 with only No. 1 fuel tank quantity gauge inoperative
Pushback from gate; all three engines started
No. 3 engine shutdown to conserve fuel due to departure delay
Aircraft becomes number four for departure; cabin prepared; No. 3 engine restarted
Cleared to taxi into position on runway 18L and hold
Cleared for takeoff on runway 18L, heading 185; AUTO PACK TRIP arming light does not illuminate
Main wheels leave ground; immediate violent rolling motion; right wing drops; captain reports two explosions; aircraft begins uncontrolled descent
Right wingtip strikes runway 900 feet beyond departure end; aircraft strikes ILS antenna array; structural breakup; post-crash fire ignites

recommendations.text: Direct principal operations inspectors to review training and operations manuals and ensure flap position verification is part of stall recovery procedures.
Require Part 121 operators to develop and use Cockpit Resource Management programs.
Perform directed engineering study of Boeing 727 takeoff warning systems.
Issue Airworthiness Directive for Boeing 727 takeoff warning system modifications.
Modify Boeing 727 checklists to verify takeoff warning system operation.

safety_changes: Boeing 727 checklists modified to verify takeoff warning system
Enhanced cockpit resource management and discipline training
